case_title: Sat Parkash v. State of Haryana and another
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance - romantic attachment; the victim's note states she loved the accused and the court refers to her not being persuaded to marry him
statutory_provisions: IPC s.363 (kidnapping); s.366 (kidnapping/forcing woman to marry, per court); s.366A (procuration of minor girl); s.376 (rape); s.302 r/w s.34 charged and acquitted; s.368 charged against co-accused
weapon: Poison (administered to the victim as alleged in the charge)
evidence_type: Suicide note (described by the court as a dying declaration); fact that victim was found at the accused's residence; admitted date-of-birth record; absence of other evidence of enticement or intercourse
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of s.302 murder charge; convicted under ss.363, 366, 366A, 368 and 376 IPC (per headnote); sentence not stated
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction upheld (Criminal Appeal No. 105-SB of 1995, judgment dated 05.01.2011)
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused kidnapped a girl of about fifteen from the lawful guardianship of her father in Ganaur on 7 June 1992, with intent that she be forced into illicit intercourse, and raped her in that area and at other places. Her date of birth was admitted as 5 November 1976. The victim was later found at the accused's residence. On 12 June 1992 it was alleged that the victim was administered poison and died, with the accused's relatives alleged to have concealed her at their house. The accused also made an attempt to commit suicide along with the victim; the victim died in that attempt while the accused survived. A note said to have been written by the victim just before the attempt was produced. In it she stated that she had left home of her own free will, that she loved the accused, and that she was taking her own life. No other evidence was produced showing that the accused enticed her away. The prosecution produced no evidence that sexual intercourse had taken place with the victim.
offence_severity: Not stated for the main offence; the judgment quotes s.366A as punishable with imprisonment up to ten years and fine; no punishment stated for ss.363, 376
physical_harm: Death of the victim (alleged poisoning; the note indicates suicide); the accused survived the attempt
number_of_offences: 4 charged (s.363, s.366A, s.376, s.302 r/w s.34 against the accused); 0 finally upheld
motive: alleged: intent to force the victim into illicit intercourse with the accused
key_evidence_accepted: Suicide note (accepted as a clear statement that the victim left home of her own free will); fact that the victim was found at the accused's residence; admitted date of birth (5.11.1976)
post_offence_conduct: Attempted suicide along with the victim (noted as undisputed)
bail_history: Enlarged on bail by the Supreme Court by motion bench order dated 15.04.2011
trial_duration: offence: 7.6.1992 (kidnapping and rape allegations), 12.6.1992 (concealment and poisoning allegations); trial judgment: not given (charges framed 18.10.1993); High Court: 05.01.2011; Supreme Court: 09.12.2015
legal_representation: Appellant: Anoop G. Chaudhary, Sr. Adv., with Suresh C. Gupta, Birendra K. Mishra, Ms. Poonam Atey. State: Deepak Thukral, Dy. AG; Arun Tewatia, Asstt. AG (for Dr. Monika Gusain); R. C. Kaushik, Advs.
investigation_status: Charge sheet filed; charges framed 18.10.1993 by Additional Sessions Judge, Sonepat; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Court considered liability under s.366 on its own motion although no express charge under s.366 was framed against the appellant
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.363, 366, 366A, 368, 376 and acquitted of murder (per headnote); High Court: conviction upheld, judgment 05.01.2011; Supreme Court: appeal allowed, accused acquitted
defence_argument: Relied on the victim's suicide note, which says she left home of her own free will, to contest the kidnapping, marriage and rape allegations
legal_principle_applied: Ingredients test for each charge: s.363 requires proof of enticement or kidnapping, presumption of kidnapping from being found at accused's house is untenable; s.366 requires persuasion or compulsion to marry; s.366A requires intent to force or seduce to illicit intercourse with another person; s.376 requires proof of sexual intercourse
